_source: St. Jude Global — Sickle Cell Outcome Grading System (SCOGS) official booklet. Grades transcribed verbatim from the outcome tables. Use grade 0 for 'present but not gradable / criteria not met' and grade -1 for 'outcome not present in note'.

Acute Sickle Cell Pain Episode.definition: A new event of pain or an exacerbation of pain lasting at least two hours with no explanation other than vaso-occlusion, requiring therapy with analgesics.
Acute Sickle Cell Pain Episode.diagnostic_criteria: Patient self-report OR care-giver proxy report for younger children, AND no explanation other than sickle cell disease.
Acute Sickle Cell Pain Episode.validation: Grade only if this is an acute vaso-occlusive pain episode. If no acute pain episode is described, return grade -1.

grades.1: Acute pain episode requiring pain treatment at HOME for pain exacerbation (no medical facility visit).
grades.2: Acute pain episode requiring a VISIT to a medical facility (including Day Hospital) for any type of pain treatment, AND NOT requiring admission.
grades.3: Acute pain episode requiring ADMISSION, AND no evidence of organ failure or any of these complications: acute chest syndrome, respiratory distress, DVT, PE, stroke, splenic sequestration, or hyperhaemolysis.
grades.4: Acute pain episode complicated with organ failure OR one of these complications (acute chest syndrome, respiratory distress, DVT, PE, stroke, splenic sequestration, hyperhaemolysis), OR resulting in a life-threatening complication requiring life-supporting treatment (mechanical ventilation, vasopressors, renal replacement therapy, or other).
grades.5: Death in the setting of acute pain episode.

Acute Chest Syndrome (ACS).definition: An acute illness characterized by fever and/or respiratory symptoms, accompanied by a NEW LOBAR pulmonary infiltrate (not atelectasis) on chest imaging.
Acute Chest Syndrome (ACS).diagnostic_criteria: Radiographic evidence of consolidation — a new segmental infiltrate involving at least one complete segment AND at least one of: temperature >= 38.5 C; >2% decrease in SpO2 from steady-state on room air; PaO2 < 60 mmHg; tachypnea; intercostal retractions / nasal flaring / accessory muscle use; thoracic pain; cough; wheezing; rales.
Acute Chest Syndrome (ACS).validation: Grade only if a new lobar/segmental infiltrate is present AND at least one qualifying sign. If no new infiltrate, return grade -1 (not gradable as ACS).

grades.1: Requires NONE of the below: supplemental oxygen, simple or exchange transfusion, erythropoietin, BiPAP, or any supportive treatment other than antibiotics.
grades.2: Requires FiO2 >21% to <50% OR simple erythrocyte transfusion, AND none of: BiPAP, high-flow O2, exchange transfusion.
grades.3: Requires >=50% FiO2 OR BiPAP OR high-flow O2 OR exchange transfusion.
grades.4: Requires >=50% FiO2 OR BiPAP OR high-flow O2 OR exchange transfusion, AND critical cardio-respiratory interventions (e.g., vasoactive/vasopressor infusions, intubation, invasive mechanical ventilation).

Acute Splenic Sequestration.definition: Rapid intrasplenic trapping of blood cells causing a precipitous fall in hemoglobin, often with thrombocytopenia and hypovolemia.
Acute Splenic Sequestration.diagnostic_criteria: Decrease in hemoglobin/hematocrit of >=20% OR a drop of >=2 g/dL from baseline, AND evidence of increased erythropoiesis (e.g. elevated reticulocyte count), AND an acutely enlarging spleen (>=2 cm from baseline).
Acute Splenic Sequestration.validation: Grade only if splenic sequestration is described. If not present, return grade -1. NOTE: Grade 2 is N/A for this outcome — never assign grade 2.

grades.1: Splenic sequestration NOT requiring any treatment.
grades.3: Splenic sequestration requiring treatment (erythrocyte transfusion, IV fluids, etc.) AND no hemodynamic instability AND not requiring splenectomy.
grades.4: Splenic sequestration AND hemodynamic instability OR requiring splenectomy.

Priapism.definition: A painful, persistent, unwanted erection of the penis, which may recur (stuttering).
Priapism.diagnostic_criteria: A painful erectile episode lasting >30 minutes, diagnosed by a physician based on patient self-report; can be confirmed by exam findings of a fully erect penis and pain in penis or scrotum.
Priapism.validation: Grade only if a priapism episode is described. If not present, return grade -1. NOTE: Grade 5 is N/A for this outcome — never assign grade 5.

grades.1: Priapism episode with or without medications at HOME, AND NOT requiring a visit to a medical facility.
grades.2: Priapism episode requiring a visit to a medical facility AND requiring treatment (e.g., medication), AND no shunt.
grades.3: Priapism episode requiring a visit to a medical facility AND requiring aspiration/irrigation, AND no shunt.
grades.4: Priapism episode requiring a visit to a medical facility AND requiring shunt surgical intervention.
